description: How an agent pays an order that waits for payment, over HTTP 402: an Audit Drive (audit) or its renewal, a Payment proof (proof), a Tool comparison (stack3, stack) or a data plan (builder, team). It gives the payment URL, the price and the rails on now (protocols; MPP: a card through a Stripe Shared Payment Token, or USDC on Tempo or Base; x402: USDC on Base). A POST to the URL with no credential answers 402 with the challenges (WWW-Authenticate for MPP, PAYMENT-REQUIRED for x402). The same request with a credential from an MPP client or x402 wallet answers with the receipt and starts the order (a data plan: your key has it at once). The price is the listed price, less a promotion code of ours given with the order; an Audit Drive adds, at cost, your paid plan if you included it and its purchase with your code. At the card checkout VAT comes on top of the price; paid over HTTP 402, the price includes any VAT. Every payment has a receipt. buyer {vat_id, country, company, address}, as the JSON body of both requests or with the order, puts your business on our invoice. Paid over HTTP 402, a data plan runs one month and doesn't renew by itself: pay again before it ends and the next month follows on. We email you 3 days before it ends. On a person's account the card checkout works too (payment.url from order). An agent's own account pays only over HTTP 402 until a person claims it. test_mode: true means Stripe's test mode: no real money moves.
